title: ID0473682-DC/Si-D/IE-[Multiple]  Connector 4 issue
description: Reported behaviour/issue: Connector 4 recurring faulted state

additional_info.subject: Galway Retail Park – Connector 4 recurring faulted state
additional_info.body:
Dear Siemens Support Team,
We are raising a new support request regarding a connector-level issue identified at our Galway Retail Park site. We are deliberately keeping this escalation strictly evidence-based, based on verified logs and observed behaviour.
Site details
Location Galway Retail Park, H91 P5Y2, Galway, Ireland
ChargePoint ID IE-GFX-E170003301
Affected connector Connector 4
Issue description
Connector 4 is repeatedly transitioning into Faulted state over short intervals. The issue appears isolated to this connector only. Other connectors on the same charge point remain operational and are not exhibiting similar behaviour.
Observed timeline
Based on OCPP StatusNotification logs:
• 20 January 2026 at 17:18 UTC – Connector 2 briefly reported Faulted state, then recovered
• 21 January 2026 between approximately 11:28 and 13:27 UTC – Connector 4 entered Faulted state multiple times, with frequent status updates recorded during this window
There is no evidence of cabinet-level faults, coordinated reboots, SECC reinitialisation, or multi-connector impact associated with these events.
Operational symptoms
• Sessions failing to start on Connector 4
• Occasional cable lock events requiring emergency release
• Users successfully redirected to other connectors
• No mid-session drops observed on other connectors
Vehicle context
Multiple vehicles were present and charging at the site during this period. At this stage, we do not have sufficient evidence to attribute the issue to a specific vehicle make or model. The fact that the fault behaviour is isolated to Connector 4, while other connectors continue to operate normally, suggests the issue may be connector-specific rather than vehicle-specific, however we are not asserting root cause and are open to Siemens’ assessment. We see 47 preparing records on this charger in the past 24 hours.
Initial assessment
At this stage, we are not asserting root cause. Based on the logs and observed behaviour, the issue appears consistent with a connector-level hardware or sensor issue rather than a backend, power, or cabinet-level fault. Possible areas for inspection may include the DC cable and handle, latch or lock mechanism, temperature or proximity sensors, or connector-specific IO components.
Actions taken
Connector 4 has been set to Unavailable to prevent further failed customer attempts. Other connectors remain live and are operating normally.
Requested support
We request Siemens support to:
• Review the connector-level diagnostics and logs for IE-GFX-E170003301-4
• Advise whether this behaviour aligns with known connector or cable failure modes
• Confirm recommended next steps, including whether on-site inspection or cable replacement is required
Please let us know if additional logs, timestamps, or vehicle identifiers would be helpful from our side.
Kind regards,
Colin

additional_info.subject: ID0473682-DC/Si-D/IE-[Multiple]  Connector 4 issue CRM:00263000382
additional_info.body:
Hi Colin! Good morning, how are you doing?
I got your ticket and just to let you know that I was trying to understand if there was any FW problem on the connector but I only realised now that you made it inoperative on purpose.
If you see on the backend that 5mins ago, the outlets went online and offline, it was because of me.
I checked the logs you mentioned regarding yesterday on DC4 and found the same behaviour from a previous ticket:
It seems that this EV, has some kind of auxiliary system or the battery voltage is getting applied on our cable and the charger to make sure there is no harm or damage to any of the participants, disables the outlet immediately.
And after the EV is plugged out, the outlet is available:
Regarding the incident on the 20th January, I find again that the customer chose the wrong connector ID:
As you can see, charger says "we can start the session but there is not cable connected to the connectorID 1", because it's connected on ID2, and as such, the charger refers to this as a authentication error and sends to the backend that it couldn't start.
Regarding the topic that the "
Occasional cable lock events requiring emergency release
" this is completely on the vehicle side. The norm of electric vehicles specifies that the
locking mechanism is always on the EV side
, as such, if there is any constraints that it's not unlocking, the fault is within the EV, we are not responsible for the lock, we only provide the "socket" for the locking mechanism to fit. I am sending a video in attachment of our own tester box so you can see for yourself, and also if you see the video, I'm clicking a button that locks/unlocks the system, the EV probably doesn't have this button since it's FW based.
In summary, I will align with the regional colleagues what to do with the connector ID 4, I must say that all the points redirect to the vehicle but I will recommend them to replace the component and confirm if we are correct or not.
As soon as someone is assigned, they will let you know.
Thank you and have a nice day ahead.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: Re: ID0473682-DC/Si-D/IE-[Multiple] Connector 4 issue CRM:00263000382
additional_info.body:
Hi All
We wanted to provide
additional information
that has come to light and which we believe is
relevant to the existing Galway Retail Park ticket currently under investigation
. -
charger 3301.
New information received
We have now received a customer complaint relating to
Galway Retail Park, connector 4
, dated Tuesday 20 January 2026 at approximately 13:40. The customer reports that a charging session did not commence, but that three separate €50 payment authorisations were taken.
Review against existing ticket
After reviewing backend logs and on-site playback for the relevant time window, we can see that connector 4 entered
Preparing
state and did not progress to an active charging session before the customer left the site. There is no evidence of a successful start or sustained charge for this attempt.
This behaviour mirrors the
same failure mode already being investigated under the current GRP ticket
, namely connector 4 entering
Preparing
and not progressing to charge, leading to abandoned sessions.
Relationship to current investigation
While the payment aspect is new, the charging behaviour itself is
not a separate or unrelated issue
, and appears to be another occurrence of the same connector-level problem already under review at Galway Retail Park.
We are therefore sharing this as
additional evidence
to be considered as part of the existing ticket, rather than raising it as a standalone incident.
Next steps
We will handle the customer refund directly. Our main concern is ensuring the underlying connector 4 issue is resolved to prevent further customer impact.
Please let us know if you need any additional timestamps or data points from our side to support the ongoing investigation.
Kind regards,
Colin
Brite Charging Limited
support@brite.ie
